batch_execution.fail_root_cause: All 30 maxwell-method FAILs are the M5 C11 (monotone mu_B) hard gate correctly rejecting the M4 spliced crust EOS, whose mu_B is non-monotone due to the M3 CLD reconstruction coarse pressure (documented in the M3 receipt: 'pressure_from_CLD'). This is NOT an M7 batch-orchestration bug; it is the upstream M3 CLD quality limitation propagating through M4 -> M5 -> M7 exactly as the fail-closed acceptance requires. The M7 orchestrator records each FAIL with error_type, error_message, and the full traceback (1500 chars) so the upstream fix is diagnosable.
batch_execution.blocked_root_cause: 210 BLOCKED tasks (7 missing crust models x 5 core x 6 methods) are recorded with the exact blocked_reason ('crust:<model>') and are NOT silently skipped. The M0 replacement ZIP staging would unblock these.

pass_task_outputs.file_hashes: 150/150 PASS tasks have SHA-256 hashes for every output file (provenance for M8/M9 validation)

criterion_2_exactly_390_unique_tasks.evidence: cardinality_check: True (manifest task_count = 390, expected_pairs = 390, 13x5x6 = 390). uniqueness_check: True (390 unique task_id hashes, 390 unique (crust,core,method) triples).

criterion_3_isolated_output_folder_and_m.evidence: 150/150 PASS tasks have an isolated output folder (cleared before each run, no cross-task contamination) and a task_receipt.json with status, timing, output file list, SHA-256 file hashes, and the method result. what_is_new_vs_m5_m5a_m6.gfortran_now_available: micromamba + conda-forge fortran-compiler installed; native Fortran backend builds and runs. This unblocks the production Fortran path for M2/M10 native kernels and the M8/M9 native validation, which were previously Python-only.
what_is_new_vs_m5_m5a_m6.batch_orchestration: M7 is the first node that exercises the full 390-task matrix end-to-end. The manifest generator + batch orchestrator pattern is the production contract: a single manifest consumed by the Fortran binary (or Python oracle here), with per-task isolation and fail-closed receipts.
what_is_new_vs_m5_m5a_m6.synthetic_core_workaround: The 5 production core models (APR/BBB/GM/RG) are not in the sandbox; synthetic polytropes stand in so the batch backend (read/write, M5/M5A) runs on real PASS paths. The synthetic cores are clearly labelled and would be replaced by the real cores once the M0 replacement ZIP is staged.

remaining_for_full_M7_completion.real_core_eos: Stage the M0 replacement ZIP (EoS_complete_core_crust_release_v3_2.zip) to provide the 5 real core CompOSE tables; this unblocks the 210 BLOCKED tasks and replaces the 5 synthetic cores with the production models.
remaining_for_full_M7_completion.m4_c11_fix_or_cld_repair: The 30 maxwell FAILs trace to the M4 spliced crust mu_B non-monotonicity (M3 CLD coarse pressure). Fixing the CLD pressure formula (M4-quality recommendation) or porting the M5 Maxwell construction to accept the legacy smootherstep policy would unblock these. Alternatively, the M5 hard gate can be relaxed to a warning for diagnostic-only runs, but the production path should keep the strict gate.
remaining_for_full_M7_completion.m2_m10_native_smooth_methods: The cubic_F/cubic_P/quintic_F/quintic_P methods are currently a stub (the legacy NPPHB Hermite bridge is not yet ported to native Fortran). Porting the smooth matcher to native Fortran (M2/M10 work) would replace the stub with a real crust-core splice for these 120 PASS tasks.
remaining_for_full_M7_completion.fortran_batch_command: The production M7 target is a Fortran batch command (compose_eos_fortran with a 'batch' action that consumes the manifest directly). This Python orchestrator is the design reference and the acceptance-validation oracle; the Fortran port would add a 'batch' action to compose_eos_fortran.f90 that reads the manifest and dispatches each task in Fortran (no Python in the production loop).

next_node_recommendation: M8 (Differential, physical and numerical validation) depends on M7. The M7 PASS task outputs (150 isolated folders with SHA-256 file hashes + transition metadata) are the M8 validation corpus. M8 would: (1) re-read each PASS output CompOSE table with the native Fortran reader and verify the C1-C11 consistency checks, (2) compare the 150 PASS outputs against the immutable v3.2 legacy 390 outputs as validation oracles (where the same pair/method exists in v3.2), (3) re-run the analytic Maxwell fixtures from M5 on the M7 maxwell outputs (the 30 FAILs are excluded; the M8 analytic fixture would use a monotone polytrope pair to validate the maxwell path independently of the M4 crust quality), (4) preserve the C1-C11, interpolation interval extrema, TOV/tidal and convergence evidence from M5/M5A/M6. The Fortran native reader/writer (now built) is the M8 validation tool.
